items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the criminal procedure law, in relation to certain domestic violence offenses
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4244               REVISED 03/29/11
TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the criminal procedure law, in relation to certain domestic
violence offenses

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
To ensure that pertinent information regarding misdemeanor crimes of
domestic violence is transmitted to the federal bureau of investigation
for purposes of determining whether a person is disqualified from
purchasing a firearm under federal law based upon conviction for certain
misdemeanor crimes of domestic violence.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
Section one amends subdivision 4 of section 170.10 of the criminal
procedure law by adding a new paragraph (f) to provide that where a
defendant is arraigned on a information, a prosecutor's information, or
a misdemeanor complaint, which contains the charges of assault or
attempted assault in the third degree, menacing or attempted menacing in
the second degree, criminal obstruction of breathing or blood
circulation or attempted criminal obstruction of breathing or
blood circulation, forcible
touching or attempted forcible touching, the people may serve upon the
defendant and file with the court a notice alleging that the defendant
(i) is a current or former spouse, parent or guardian of
the victim, or (ii) shares
a child in common with such person, or (iii)is cohabiting or has
cohabitated
with the victim as a spouse, parent, or guardian, or (iv) is or was
similarly
situated to a spouse, parent or guardian of the victim. The section
further
provides that a defendant may stipulate or admit in the course of a plea
disposition that he or she is related or situated to the victim as
described
in which case the relationship shall be deemed established. If the
defendant
denies such relationship to the victim as alleged in the,notice served
by the people, the people shall have the burden of proving
that the defendant is related or situated to the victim as
alleged beyond a reasonable doubt during
the trial. The trier of fact shall make a determination with respect
to such allegation orally on the record or in writing.

Section two amends section 180.10 of the criminal procedure law by
adding new subdivisions 1(b) and 1(c) to provide that where a felony
complaint which contains the charges of assault or attempted assault in
the third degree, menacing or attempted menacing in the second degree,
criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation or attempted
criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation, forcible
touching or
attempted forcible touching, the people may serve upon the defendant
and file
with the court a notice alleging that the defendant is a current or
former
spouse, parent, or guardian of the victim, or shares a child in common


with
such person, or (iii) is cohabitating or has cohabitated with the
victim as a
spouse, parent, or guardian, or (iv) is or was similarly situated to a
spouse, parent or guardian of the victim, and thereafter follow the same
procedures set forth in new Section 170.10(4) (f) above.

Section three amends section 210.15 of the criminal procedure
law by adding a new subdivision (d) to provide where an indictment which
contains the charges of assault or attempted assault in the third
degree, menacing or attempted menacing in the second degree, criminal
obstruction of breathing or blood circulation or attempted criminal
obstruction of breathing or blood circulation, forcible touching or
attempted forcible touching, the people may serve upon the defendant and
file with the court a notice alleging that the defendant (i) is a
current or former spouse, parent or guardian of the victim, or (ii)
shares a child in common with such person, or (iii) is cohabiting or has
cohabitated with the victim as a spouse, parent, or guardian, or (iv) is
or was similarly situated to a spouse, parent or guardian of the victim,
and thereafter follow the same procedures set forth in new Section
170.10(4) (f) above.

Section four amends the criminal procedure Law by adding new section
380.97 which provides that upon judgment of conviction of the offenses
specified
above the clerk of the court shall notify DCJS of the determination
that has been made about the status of the defendant as a current
or former spouse of
the victim, parent or guardian of the victim, sharing a child in
common with
such the victim or is cohabiting or has cohabitated with the victim as a
spouse, parent, or guardian, or is or was similarly situated to a
spouse, parent or guardian of the victim.

JUSTIFICATION:
Keeping firearms out of the hands of individuals convicted of certain
violent
misdemeanors is of great importance to the citizens of this state. In
Dutchess County alone there have been four recent instances of deaths
due to
domestic violence in the past year. These tragic events highlight the
volatility of domestic violence cases and require action to ensure
that an
already dangerous situation is not compounded by allowing individuals
convicted of certain misdemeanors access to legal firearms. This bill
closes a potential gap in the reporting of crimes by our state to
the federal government and ensures that individuals convicted of certain
misdemeanors are barred from purchasing firearms legally.

Currently, a federal firearms licensee
(FFL) may not sell or otherwise dispose of a firearm to a person who has
been convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence (MCDV). The
Criminal Justice Information Services Division of the Federal Bureau of
Investigation (FBI) National Instant Criminal Background Check System
(NICS) determines firearm eligibility by conducting a background check,
which includes a check of automated databases. In cases where additional
information is needed, follow-up requests are made to agencies such as


the police, prosecutors or the courts; the NICS has three business days
to determine whether a proposed gun transfer is prohibited. If the NICS
has not been able to make a definitive determination within three busi-
ness days, the FFL may lawfully transfer the firearm.

An MCDV is defined under federal law as an offense that: (i) is a
misdemeanor under federal, state or tribal law (ii) has as an
element the use
or attempted use of physical force, or the threatened use of a deadly
weapon; and (iii) at the time the offense was committed, the defendant
was (A) a current or former spouse, parent, or guardian of the victim;
(B) a person with whom the victim shares a child in common; (C) a person
who is cohabiting with or has cohabitated with the victim as a spouse,
parent, or guardian; or (D) a person who was or is similarly situated to
a spouse, parent, or guardian of the victim.

Two critical pieces of information that would enable the
FBI to determine whether a person has been convicted of an MCDV under
federal law and therefore disqualified from purchasing a firearm are not
provided by the State to the FBI.

This bill will provide the mechanism by which the two critical pieces of
information may be transmitted by the State to the FBI. The bill identi-
fies specific misdemeanor offenses that have the requisite element of
the use of or attempted use of physical force or the threatened use of a
deadly weapon and therefore satisfy one of the criteria under federal
law to constitute an MCDV. In the case of those offenses, the bill
provides the people with the ability to determine at trial the relation-
ship of the defendant to the victim as described and therefore satisfy
the second of the criteria required under federal law to constitute an
MCDV. If the relationship as described is determined as provided in the
bill, such relationship will be noted on the defendant's record, which
record is transmitted by DCJS to the FBI for purposes of NICS.

With this critical information in the NICS, if a defendant has been
convicted of an MCDV, the NICS can deny the firearm application without
further research, resulting in greater efficiencies in conducting back-
ground checks and less delay in making determinations as to the eligi-
bility to acquire a firearm, better ensuring that an individual who is
prohibited under federal law from acquiring a firearm does not acquire
the firearm. By failing to transmit this critical information, we run
the risk that individuals who are prohibited from buying a gun neverthe-
less can because we did not give the FBI the necessary information that
requires us to keep the guns out of their hands.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATION:
None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of November next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the criminal procedure law, in relation to certain domestic violence offenses
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4244B

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the criminal procedure law, in relation to certain domestic
violence offenses

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
To ensure that pertinent information regarding misdemeanor crimes of
domestic violence is transmitted to the federal bureau of
investigation for purposes of determining whether a person is
disqualified from purchasing a firearm under federal law based upon
conviction for certain misdemeanor crimes of domestic violence

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

370.15 to provide that when a defendant has been charged with assault
or attempted assault in the third degree, menacing or attempted
menacing in the second degree, criminal obstruction of breathing or
blood circulation or attempted criminal obstruction of breathing or
blood circulation, forcible touching or attempted forcible touching,
the people may, at arraignment or no later than 15 days after
arraignment, for the purpose of notifying the division of criminal
justice services as described in section two below, serve upon the
defendant and file with the court a notice alleging that the
defendant is related or situated to the victim of the crime in the
manner specified in 18 U.S.C. 921(a)(33)(A)(ii). The notice must
include the name of the person alleged to be the victim of the
offense, specify the nature of the alleged relationship as set forth
in 18 U.S.C.
921(a)(33)(A)(ii), and set forth specific facts supporting such
allegation. Upon conviction to such offense, the court must advise
the defendant that he or she is entitled to a hearing on the
allegation contained in the notice and, if necessary, an adjournment
of the sentencing
proceeding in order to prepare for such hearing, and that if such
allegation is sustained, that determination and conviction will be
reported to the division of criminal justice services. The section
further provides that a defendant may stipulate or admit orally on
the record or in writing that he or she is related or situated to the
victim as described in this section, in which case the relationship
shall be deemed established for the purpose set forth in section two
below.
If the defendant denies such relationship to the victim as alleged in
the notice served by the people, the people shall have the burden of
proving beyond a reasonable doubt that the defendant is related or
situated to the victim as alleged in the notice. At the conclusion of
the hearing, or upon such a stipulation or admission, as applicable,
the court shall make a specific written determination with respect to
such allegation.

380.97 to provide that upon judgment of conviction of assault or
attempted assault in the third degree, menacing or attempted menacing
in the second degree, criminal obstruction of breathing or blood
circulation or attempted criminal obstruction of breathing or blood


circulation, forcible touching or attempted forcible touching, and
the defendant has been determined to be related or situated to the
victim of the offense in the manner specified in 18 U.S.C. 921
(a)(33)(A)(ii), the clerk of the court shall include notification and
a copy of the written determination in any report of such conviction
to the division of criminal justice services to enable the division
to report such determination to the federal bureau of investigation
and assist the bureau to identify persons prohibited from purchasing
and possessing a firearm pursuant to the provisions of 18 U.S.C. 922.

Section three provides the effective date.

prohibited. If the NICS has not been able to make a definitive
determination within three business days, the FFL may lawfully

This is a new bill.

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred and twentieth day
after it shall become a law.
